claims.text: The initial material is a tungsten-based refractory high-entropy alloy produced using stepwise controllable coherent nanoprecipitation.
The initial tungsten alloy contains no intentionally incorporated lubricious phase.
Introducing controlled WS2 nanoprecipitates into a tungsten RHEA will produce in situ self-lubricating behavior.
WS2 can be formed as coherent nanoprecipitates within the tungsten matrix.
The proposed WS2 nanoprecipitates can form a layered lubricious structure at the alloy surface.
WS2 nanoprecipitates can coexist with the strengthening features of the tungsten RHEA.
Stepwise controllable coherent nanoprecipitation can provide a tungsten RHEA with ultrahigh strength and tensile ductility.
Coherent precipitate interfaces facilitate dislocation transmission and relieve stress concentrations that could initiate premature cracks.
Tungsten RHEAs strengthened through coherent nanoprecipitation can retain substantial mechanical strength at 800 degrees Celsius.
WS2 acts as a solid lubricant because its layered crystal structure facilitates easy shear.
Combining WS2 lubrication with nanoprecipitation-strengthened tungsten will balance the strength-lubrication trade-off.
The modified alloy will maintain low friction and wear over a wide temperature span.
Relative to the WS2-free baseline, the modified alloy will have a lower friction coefficient.
The modified alloy will show stable tribological performance across temperatures extending to approximately 800 degrees Celsius or higher.
Adding WS2 nanoprecipitates will not sacrifice the high strength and ductility of the baseline alloy.
The baseline tungsten RHEA exhibits high strength.
The baseline tungsten RHEA has suboptimal self-lubricating performance under extreme or variable-temperature conditions.
At very high temperatures in strongly oxidizing environments, WS2 may deteriorate and compromise lubrication.
